stem.text: Use the direct comparison test to determine whether the series \( \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} a_n \), where \( a_n = \frac{n^{\frac{2}{3}} + 2}{n^{\frac{4}{3}}} \), converges or diverges. Verify the conditions of the test.

answer_key.label: The series diverges by the direct comparison test, because \( a_n \ge \frac{1}{n^{\frac{2}{3}}} \text{ and } p = \frac{2}{3} \le 1 \).

worked_solution.text: The terms are positive, so the direct comparison test applies. Compare with \( \sum \frac{1}{n^{\frac{2}{3}}} \), the p-series with \( p = \frac{2}{3} \).

Splitting the fraction, \( \frac{n^{\frac{2}{3}} + 2}{n^{\frac{4}{3}}} = \frac{1}{n^{\frac{2}{3}}} + \frac{2}{n^{\frac{4}{3}}} \), so \( \frac{n^{\frac{2}{3}} + 2}{n^{\frac{4}{3}}} \ge \frac{1}{n^{\frac{2}{3}}} > 0 \) for every n.
The series diverges by the direct comparison test, because \( a_n \ge \frac{1}{n^{\frac{2}{3}}} \text{ and } p = \frac{2}{3} \le 1 \), so \( \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} a_n \) diverges.

options.label: The series converges by the alternating series test, because \( a_n \) decreases to 0.
options.derivation: the alternating series test named for a series of positive terms, its alternating hypothesis never checked

options.label: The series diverges by the direct comparison test, because \( a_n \le \frac{1}{n^{\frac{2}{3}}} \text{ and } p = \frac{2}{3} \le 1 \).
options.derivation: the comparison inequality written the other way round, which cannot show divergence

options.label: The series diverges by the direct comparison test, because \( a_n \ge \frac{1}{n^{\frac{2}{3}}} \text{ and } p = \frac{2}{3} \le 1 \).
The series converges by the nth term test, because \( \lim_{n\to\infty} a_n = 0 \).
options.derivation: convergence concluded because the terms approach 0
